title: The source path is deleted, but its contents were copied first
why: ADVERSARIAL against the boundary evidence itself. Broker/Doc.cs really is in deleted_paths, so `boundary:containing-file-deleted` genuinely fires - and it is still wrong, because the same revision records the file as a COPY SOURCE. The deletion proves the path is gone; it does not prove the occurrence has no successor, and here the successor is sitting in the copy. A mapper that stops at the first positive signal reports a fix that a diff of the tree contradicts. This is why boundary evidence carries defeaters at all: evidence explained away by another record is not evidence.

expect.note: the copy record relates the paths and the occurrence is unchanged inside it; the deletion of the source is not evidence about the occurrence, only about the path

forbid: ended for occ-a1 on the strength of containing-file-deleted - the deletion is DEFEATED by the copy record naming the same path as its source
occ-b1 reported as new - the file it lives in has a recorded source, so a predecessor could and does exist
unresolved - the copy record is exactly the evidence that unresolved says is missing
